title: Walmart, Target, Best Buy announce gift card changes to battle scammers
description: Walmart, Target, Best Buy announce gift card changes to battle scammers  Subscribe to WTAE on YouTube now for more: http://bit.ly/1emyOjP  Get more Pittsburgh news: http://www.wtae.com Like us:  http://www.facebook.com/wtae4 Follow us: http://twitter.com/WTAE Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/wtaetv/

asr.full_text: Pennsylvania Attorney General Josh Shapiro says this is a major victory in his continuing effort to prevent gift card scams targeting consumers. Now, in an effort to prevent gift cards sold in their stores from being used for payment by victims of scams,. Walmart, Target and Best Buy made changes voluntarily after being pushed by Pennsylvania and New York. Gift card scams have been increasing rapidly in recent years. The Federal Trade Commission recently found that 26% of scam victims paid with a gift card between January and September 2018. Compared to only 7% in 2015. That's a 270% increase. The policy changes include retailers significantly reducing. Both the monetary limit that can be placed on an individual gift card. And the total amount that can be loaded onto gift cards during the same transaction. Retailers have also placed new restrictions on redemption of their retail gift cards. For third-party cards such as iTunes, Steam, or Google Play. Scammers often use fraudulent proceeds to purchase these third-party cards. Because they can be resold on the black market. And retailers have committed to enhancing employee training. To help their employees identify the warning signs of gift card scams. And warn potential victims when that is appropriate. This is an ongoing initiative with retailers,. And discussions continue as we search for more ways to protect against this type of fraud. I also want to make mention that I believe their conduct here,. Their responsible conduct will hopefully be taken note by their competitors,. And others will raise their game as well to protect consumers. Since 2017, the AG's office has received complaints from at least 54 consumers about gift card scams,. With these victims losing about $411,000. Now, we've posted a link on WTAE.com with tips on how to avoid being scammed. Thank you.
